text: No warm-up. The serpent's head slams down on Borro's shield, and Nib goes for its neck.
His knives skid off the jade scales in a shower of sparks.
Nib lands and checks his blades: chipped. The serpent hasn't even noticed.
Then it blasts steam until Borro's shield glows red and his moss smokes.
Carry moves burns too. Blisters rise on Jaeha's palms.
Its coils slide toward the fish section, the tail dragging through ice.
Frost spreads over the scales, and the tail jerks away as if burned.
Jaeha watches that tail, and his eyes narrow.
His palms are too burned to hold the notebook, so Yerin holds it for him.
He calls his sister, who knows this market better than he does, keys and dead ends included.
A dead end is exactly what he wants: one way in, and a giant for the door.
Yerin grabs his vest; he's in no state for this. He'll do what he's done for four years.
He runs past its head, a warm body behind a red-hot shield. It takes the bait.
The kimchi granny and her son haul the freezers open; Seoa, rice cakes still on her wrist, kicks open a truck.
Forty metres of freezers and mist, ending in a wall, and the serpent follows him in.
Where its hot scales meet the cold, the whole lane fills with fog.
Frost creeps over the jade and gold. The steam thins.
Jaeha runs out of lane, back to the frozen wall. The jaws rise over him, slower now.
Cornered, he gives the jaws the polite smile every raid leader got for four years.
Behind it, Borro wedges his shield across the lane's mouth. Now it's locked in with the cold.
It thrashes, smashing doors and trucks, but every move is slower than the last.
Its frozen tail hammers Borro's shield, and Jaeha feels every blow from the far end.
Its yellow eye goes cloudy. Only the violet crack on its brow still pulses.
The cold did what knives couldn't. With thirty seconds on Nib's clock, Jaeha points at the one spot that matters.
Nib runs up the serpent's frozen coils like a staircase.
Both knives go through the frosted scales, which shatter like ice, right into the crack.
The serpent rears, smashes the lights, and bursts into violet ash and glittering frost.
Ash and frost settle like snow. Jaeha slides down the wall to sit.
Where it fell, a violet core floats in the air, and the break starts to seal.
The next window values the core at thirty million won. He gives it a long, tired look.
Three in a row with no release button, and he doesn't like it. He presses it anyway.
The core drops into his blistered hands: level five, a third summon slot, and Route Alignment at ninety.
The real hunters arrive at last and give Borro a wide berth. The core goes to a relief fund; Jaeha only asks about the bridge.
By morning, a whole subway car is watching Bomi's upload, titled for him without asking: His Summons Go First.
Everywhere, people watch a husk hold up a bridge and argue about whether it's real.
Even the news can't quite bring itself to say what they are.
At school, Seoa is famous by association, and admits to having a brother with great reluctance.
The kimchi granny holds a radish up to the TV cameras like a trophy, claiming her share.
Then Bomi's subscriber count crosses the line she has been chasing: one hundred thousand.
She screams at the sky outside her parents' restaurant, open for the first time in weeks.
That's the number that saves the family restaurant. One drone was a small price.
Back on the rooftop, Bomi has a new drone and a thumbnail to shoot. Borro poses.
Nib does not smile on request, and certainly not for an algorithm.
Bomi pushes his mouth into a smile with two fingers. His eyes stay dead.
So she puts his refusal in the title.
Yerin cools his blistered palm with a soda can. The rookie who froze on her first raid is proud of herself, and so is he.
That evening, a crowd outside the market chants Trap Rats, the name guilds used to spit at him.
Not everyone is cheering. High in Kanghan Tower, one window is still lit.
At last, the man in silver glasses shows his face: Director Baek Taegun, who wanted to know which survivor it was.
Now he knows: the trap-tester who should be dead is ninety-one percent likely to be an Operator.
He replays the bridge clip and sees what the internet missed: the giant chose.
One call, smiling with his mouth only: Black Hound will offer the hero a big raid, and watch what protects him.
In its glass case, a boss core pulses slowly, like a heartbeat.
In Kanghan's guild hall, forty flawless husks hold one lunge in perfect rows, under a woman's silver baton.
She turns from them all in white, as if she owns the hall. A husk holds out the clip.
On it, a masked shape moves too fast. Her half-smile freezes. She commands forty husks; she knows their limits.
One flick of her baton, and all forty heads turn to look.
Friday night, Jaeha sneezes all over his tteokbokki, as if someone were talking about him.
Borro's welcome dinner, at last. He sits on the roof to be level with everyone, beside his new sprout.
Borro examines a single rice cake gravely. Seoa carried these across a falling bridge, so he'd better like them.
He chews very, very slowly. On Monday it was probably. The verdict is in.
Then his phone buzzes. Mok, who locked him in with a boss, invites him on a raid as a hero.
The laughter's gone. Seoa answers before he can. Yerin was locked in with him, and hasn't forgotten.
Nib's ears go flat. A scout who was left behind knows the type.
Bomi says what the whole city can see. Jaeha turns his pencil. Spotting traps is his career.
He sketches what he expects: a hound's-head shield, a crossbow, a door with a lamp. He's seen this one before.
His eyes go cold and level.
The notebook snaps shut. That means the plan is ready.
For once, the trap-tester stands up straight. He's accepting, and this time he isn't the one walking into it.
